strings.d1.s0.name: War Remnants Museum
strings.d1.s0.tips: A museum on the Vietnam War: heavy but important. Go in the cool of the morning.
strings.d1.s1.name: Independence Palace
strings.d1.s1.tips: The palace the tanks rolled into in 1975. Look for the 1960s architecture and the bunker.
strings.d1.s2.name: Notre-Dame Cathedral Saigon
strings.d1.s2.tips: A French-built cathedral (under restoration), with the Central Post Office opposite.
strings.d1.s3.name: Pho Hoa Pasteur
strings.d1.s3.tips: A classic serving pho since 1968, on Pasteur Street.
strings.d1.s4.name: Ben Thanh Market
strings.d1.s4.tips: The city's emblematic market: coffee, dried mango, and bargaining is a must.
strings.d1.b0.name: Banh Mi Huynh Hoa
strings.d1.b0.tips: Saigon's most famous banh mi, with 10 kinds of meat. Expect a queue.
strings.d1.b1.name: Saigon Central Post Office
strings.d1.b1.tips: The post office designed by Eiffel. Step inside to see it.
strings.d2.s0.name: Cu Chi Tunnels Ben Duoc
strings.d2.s0.tips: 1.5 hours from the city (tour ~500,000 VND, or bus no. 13). A 200 km tunnel network; Ben Duoc is less touristy. Expect 20-100 m of crawling.
strings.d2.s1.name: Cu Chi Tapioca Tasting
strings.d2.s1.tips: At the tunnel exit, try war-era tapioca and tea. Included in the tour.
strings.d2.s2.name: Cu Chi Local Eatery
strings.d2.s2.tips: Com tam (broken rice) on the way back.
strings.d2.s3.name: Jade Emperor Pagoda
strings.d2.s3.tips: Saigon's most atmospheric temple, with a turtle pond and incense smoke.
strings.d2.s4.name: Nguyen Hue Walking Street
strings.d2.s4.tips: A pedestrian boulevard in front of City Hall, with the cafes of Cafe Apartment (42 Nguyen Hue).
strings.d2.b0.name: Cafe Apartment Saigon
strings.d2.b0.tips: A nine-storey apartment block full of cafes, with balcony views.
strings.d2.b1.name: Ho Chi Minh City Museum
strings.d2.b1.tips: The city's history. An alternative to the pagoda.
strings.d3.s0.name: Binh Tay Market
strings.d3.s0.tips: Cho Lon's wholesale market: lively in the morning, with street breakfast.
strings.d3.s1.name: Thien Hau Temple
strings.d3.s1.tips: A temple to the sea goddess, hung with spiral incense coils.
strings.d3.s2.name: Cho Lon Street Food Tour
strings.d3.s2.tips: Hu tieu (Cho Lon noodle soup) and dim sum on Ha Ton Quyen Street.
strings.d3.s3.name: Cha Tam Church
strings.d3.s3.tips: The church where Diem was captured, in Cho Lon.
strings.d3.s4.name: Bui Vien Walking Street
strings.d3.s4.tips: The backpacker street: beer on plastic stools, and plenty of noise.
strings.d3.b0.name: Com Tam Ba Ghien
strings.d3.b0.tips: The city's most famous com tam, in Phu Nhuan.
strings.d3.b1.name: Saigon Opera House
strings.d3.b1.tips: Home of the A O Show bamboo circus. An alternative to Bui Vien.
strings.d4.s0.name: Tan Dinh Church
strings.d4.s0.tips: The pink-painted cathedral. Good for photos.
strings.d4.s1.name: Tan Dinh Market
strings.d4.s1.tips: A local market, good for a banh cuon breakfast.
strings.d4.s2.name: Vietnam Coffee Tour Cong Caphe
strings.d4.s2.tips: Coconut coffee at Cong Caphe, plus egg coffee.
strings.d4.s3.name: Turtle Lake
strings.d4.s3.tips: The Turtle Lake roundabout, popular with young locals and street snacks.
strings.d4.s4.name: Secret Garden Restaurant Saigon
strings.d4.s4.tips: Vietnamese home cooking in a rooftop garden, in District 1.
strings.d4.b0.name: Banh Xeo 46A
strings.d4.b0.tips: Vietnamese crispy pancakes on Dinh Cong Trang.
strings.d4.b1.name: Fine Arts Museum Saigon
strings.d4.b1.tips: Art in a colonial mansion. An alternative to the coffee stop.
strings.d5.s0.name: My Tho Vinh Trang Pagoda
strings.d5.s0.tips: 1.5 hours from the city (tour ~600,000 VND, lunch included). Look for the giant Buddhas.
strings.d5.s1.name: Mekong River Boat Tour
strings.d5.s1.tips: A boat on the main river, with stops at Unicorn Island and honey and coconut candy workshops.
strings.d5.s2.name: Ben Tre Canoe Tour
strings.d5.s2.tips: A sampan ride through palm-lined canals. Included in the tour.
strings.d5.s3.name: Mekong Island Restaurant
strings.d5.s3.tips: Elephant ear fish and rice paper rolls. Included in the tour.
strings.d5.s4.name: Ben Tre Coconut Workshop
strings.d5.b0.name: Cai Be Floating Market
strings.d5.b0.tips: A morning floating market, instead of My Tho (early start).
strings.d5.b1.name: My Tho Hu Tieu Restaurant
strings.d5.b1.tips: My Tho noodle soup. An alternative to the island stop.
strings.d6.s0.name: Bitexco Saigon Skydeck
strings.d6.s0.tips: Views from the 49th floor, clearest in the morning.
strings.d6.s1.name: Ho Thi Ky Flower Market
strings.d6.s1.tips: A flower market with Cambodian street food, in District 10.
strings.d6.s2.name: Ho Thi Ky Cambodian Noodles
strings.d6.s2.tips: Num banh chok (Khmer rice noodles), inside the market.
strings.d6.s3.name: Landmark 81 SkyView
strings.d6.s3.tips: Vietnam's tallest building, in Binh Thanh.
strings.d6.s4.name: Thu Thiem Riverside
strings.d6.s4.tips: The city skyline at sunset from the new bridge, with cafes nearby.
strings.d6.b0.name: Quan Ut Ut Thu Thiem
strings.d6.b1.name: Saigon Water Bus
strings.d6.b1.tips: The river bus from Bach Dang. A cheap alternative to Landmark.
strings.d7.theme: Morning market and a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Tao Dan Park
strings.d7.s0.tips: Morning tai chi and birdcage coffee: the city's daily ritual.
strings.d7.s1.name: Pho Le
strings.d7.s1.tips: Sweet-style pho in District 5. A farewell breakfast.
strings.d7.s2.name: Saigon Square
strings.d7.s2.tips: Cheap clothing and souvenirs, and air-conditioned.
strings.d7.s3.name: L'Usine Le Loi
strings.d7.s3.tips: A cafe-boutique for coffee and pastries. A last farewell stop.
strings.d7.s4.name: Tan Son Nhat Airport Bus 109
strings.d7.s4.tips: The bus to the airport takes 30 minutes. Farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Banh Mi 37 Nguyen Trai
strings.d7.b0.tips: Banh mi with grilled meatballs, from a street cart.
strings.d7.b1.name: Saigon Botanical Garden
strings.d7.b1.tips: A botanical garden and zoo. An alternative to the park.
strings.note0: Grab (motorbike or car) is cheap and safe; a motorbike taxi costs 30,000-60,000 VND. Metro Line 1 (Ben Thanh-Suoi Tien) is open.
strings.note1: May to October is the rainy season: expect an hour-long downpour every afternoon, so sightsee in the morning. It is 32°C and humid.
strings.note2: Pho costs 60-90,000 VND, banh mi 30-60,000, coffee 30-60,000. Street stools are safe, and the ice is factory-made.
strings.note3: A tour (hotel pick-up included) is the most practical way to do Cu Chi and the Mekong. The Ben Duoc tunnels are quieter than Ben Dinh.
strings.note4: Cross the road at a steady pace (the motorbikes will go around you), and don't hold your phone in your hand on the street, as bag snatchers operate.
strings.note5: Tipping is not expected; bargain 30-50% off in markets.
